title: Decision card
description: Plan 7.3. A frozen checkpoint decision: the question, two to six bounded options, the evidence references, the affected artifact hashes, two independent supervisor judgments, a deterministic authority check and the ruling. Agreement is not authority, and the schema says so structurally: a 'decided' ruling requires the authority check to have passed with the charter permitting the action, the required evidence present and the seats independent — matching judgments alone never satisfy it (release scenario 16). There is no third judgment: 'judgments' is capped at two, because adding a tie-breaking supervisor to avoid asking the human is exactly what plan 7.3 forbids, and a missing supervisor blocks rather than being replaced by the implementer (release scenario 17). Disagreement, missing evidence, a supervisor failure or an out-of-charter action blocks the checkpoint and emits one escalation.

checkpoint.description: The checkpoint category being decided. It must be one the charter lists; a category outside the charter is not theirs to decide (plan 7.2, 7.3).

question.description: The one question this card settles. A card with two questions is two cards.

options.description: Bounded options, two to six. Reusing common#/$defs/option keeps a decision card and an escalation speaking the same vocabulary (plan 7.4).

evidence.description: The evidence references the judgments are made on. Required evidence being present is a precondition of authority, not a courtesy (plan 7.3).

required_evidence.description: What this checkpoint category needs before it can be decided at all. Fail closed when required evidence is absent (AGENTS.md). Where the evaluator named in advance is a human — a prototype whose question is about human experience is the case plan 11 names — that human's judgment is required evidence: absent, 'required_evidence_present' is false, the authority check fails, and the checkpoint blocks with one escalation rather than an automated verdict standing in for the experience the prototype exists to produce (ruling `prototype-human-experience-needs-human`, release scenario 4). Which questions are about human experience is not decidable from this document; naming the evaluator in advance is what makes it checkable.

affected_artifacts.description: The artifacts this decision binds, by id and hash. Freezing the hashes is what stops a decision drifting onto a changed artifact (plan 5.2, 7.3).

charter.description: The charter this decision is taken under, bound by hash, plus the rule that makes the checkpoint decidable.

seats.description: Exactly two supervisor seats, declared independent. Independence is a structural constraint on the seating that the runner enforces; it is never a property of who or what fills a seat. Neither seat may be the implementer or the approver of the work under decision (plan 7.3). A seat that cannot be filled independently is unavailable and blocks the checkpoint; it is never backfilled by the implementer, the author, the spec approver or a seat already on the panel (ruling `missing-supervisor-never-implementer`, release scenario 17).

judgments.description: One judgment per seat, at most two in total. Each returns a choice, a concise rationale, the assumptions it could not resolve, and an escalation flag (plan 7.3). A missing judgment is a blocked checkpoint, never a seat filled by someone else (release scenario 17).

choice.description: The id of one of the bounded options. A judgment cannot invent an option.

unresolved_assumptions.description: Present but empty means the seat resolved everything it needed. Absent would mean the seat was never asked.

saw_other_judgment.description: Always false: independence comes from isolated evidence packets, not from sequential scheduling (plan 6.5, 7.3).

agreement.description: Whether the two judgments chose the same option. Recorded as a fact and never as a source of authority: agreement is necessary and never sufficient, and it supports a decision only when the authority check below also passes (plan 7.3, release scenario 16, ruling `supervisor-agreement-is-not-authority`). Confidence is off the authority path entirely; the charter and the evidence carry it.

authority_check.description: The deterministic policy check (plan 7.3). It is performed by policy against artifact evidence, not by a judgment, and every component is recorded so a failure names itself. Confidence alone cannot grant authority; absent required evidence fails closed. 'charter_permits' and 'checkpoint_in_charter' are what make a sensitive action decidable at all: the charter entry a human approved up front, naming the action and its scope, is the permission, and the pair may never enlarge its own authority mid-run (ruling `sensitive-actions-need-approved-charter-entry`, release scenario 5).

allOf.description: A passing authority check is a conjunction, not a summary: every component holds or the result is 'fail'.

ruling.description: The outcome. 'decided' requires the authority check to have passed; 'blocked' is the result for disagreement, missing evidence, a supervisor failure or an out-of-charter action, and it carries one escalation rather than another round of internal debate (plan 7.3, release scenario 16).

chosen_option.description: The option id that was decided, or null when blocked.

recorded_by.description: Who recorded the outcome. The enum admits only the policy check and the runner: accepting a decision record is not an authority a skill has (ruling `central-kb-owns-project-artifacts`, docs/decisions/0001-kb-document-vocabulary.md). The decision is project-derived material the central knowledgebase owns; this artifact carries the ruling, and no skill makes a repository-local documentation tree its home instead.

escalation.description: One escalation, emitted once. Plan 7.4's shape: the single decision needed, the bounded options, the evidence already gathered, the recommended default, the triggering charter rule and the blocked ticket or finding.

grants_issued.description: Grants that follow from a 'decided' ruling. Skills never issue grants; the runner does, and each one binds to the charter hash (common#/$defs/grant_ref, AGENTS.md).

allOf.description: Agreement is not authority. A decided ruling requires both judgments returned and the deterministic authority check passed on every component; two seats choosing the same option is necessary and by itself never sufficient (plan 7.3, release scenario 16).
A blocked ruling carries exactly one escalation and no chosen option. One escalation, not repeated internal debate and not a third seat (plan 7.3, release scenarios 16 and 17).
Disagreement blocks. There is no tie-break and no further round (plan 7.3).
A seat that failed to return blocks the checkpoint. It is not filled by the implementer, and it is not covered by the seat that did return (release scenario 17).
A judgment raising the escalation flag stops the checkpoint rather than being outvoted (plan 7.3).
Grants follow only from a decided ruling. A blocked checkpoint issues nothing (plan 7.1, 7.3).
